note: Stratified by teacher confidence (15 high, 20 medium, 5 low) to oversample the most concerning case: confident disagreements.

categories.gold_noise: Teacher's answer is clearly better supported by the narrative text than gold; NHTSA's raw label looks wrong or internally inconsistent with how NHTSA codes near-identical narratives elsewhere.
categories.subtype_ambiguity: Both answers sit in the same real cluster of adjacent/overlapping systems (e.g. ENGINE vs ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING vs POWER TRAIN; STEERING vs SUSPENSION at the axle/tie-rod/hub boundary) where the physical boundary itself is fuzzy, not a modeling error.
categories.multi_issue_ambiguity: Narrative genuinely describes multiple distinct problems; teacher and gold anchored on different ones, both defensibly.
categories.unknowable_from_text: Correct label depends on info not in the narrative (usually a linked recall campaign's official system code, or an ODINO sibling row) -- confirmed directly in one case where the complainant literally quotes the recall's assigned category name.
categories.teacher_clean_miss: Genuine teacher error -- gold is right, teacher overreached instead of using UNKNOWN OR OTHER or picked a poor-fit category.

rows.note: Wheel hub separated from vehicle -- WHEELS vs SUSPENSION, the hub sits on both systems' boundary.

Windshield spontaneously cracked (no wiper involved) but gold=VISIBILITY/WIPER. See 135030/407854: NHTSA's own coding of VISIBILITY vs VISIBILITY/WIPER is inconsistent in BOTH directions, not a learnable rule.
Literal wiper failure ('windshield wipers become inoperative') but gold=VISIBILITY (not the WIPER variant). Opposite-direction confirmation that this category pair is just noisy in the raw data.
Same pattern: literal wiper failure, gold=VISIBILITY not VISIBILITY/WIPER.
Narrative is 100% about an EV HV-battery recall notice mishandling; zero steering content. gold=STEERING almost certainly comes from the linked recall's official system code.
'Death wobble' + tie rod recalls -- classic STEERING/SUSPENSION boundary case for front-end wobble.
Crankshaft/camshaft sensor causing stall -- textbook ENGINE, no connection to gold's VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL.
Single recall disables airbags, seat belt pretensioners, AND side airbags simultaneously -- AIR BAGS (teacher) vs SEAT BELTS (gold) both defensible.
Child door lock mechanism stuck -- exactly matches LATCHES/LOCKS/LINKAGES definition; gold=STRUCTURE has no support in text.
Water pump defect -> overheating -- textbook ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING; gold=FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM unsupported.
'Whole transmission needs to be fixed' -- clear POWER TRAIN signal; gold=UNKNOWN OR OTHER looks like a miss.
EGR sensor failure -- ENGINE vs ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING boundary (documented cluster).
'Power steering cuts out' explicitly stated -- clear STEERING signal; gold=ELECTRONIC STABILITY CONTROL unsupported by text.

Spark plug replaced 18x -- checked against full dataset: ENGINE is the dominant code for spark-plug narratives (4,557 rows) vs ELECTRICAL SYSTEM (2,058) -- real ~14% minority pattern, not a prompt error. Confirms our prompt's ENGINE mapping is well-calibrated to the majority convention.
Transmission cracked/overheated -- ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING/POWER TRAIN documented confusion cluster.

Heater splitter door failure -- compare to 1335413 (heater blowing cold air) which gold codes as VISIBILITY/WIPER. Same underlying HVAC issue type coded two different ways by NHTSA -- inconsistent, not a learnable rule.
'Engine fell out' (symptom) vs subframe bolts not tightened (root cause) -- STRUCTURE vs ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING, both readings defensible.

5 distinct problems in one narrative (wiper -- already fixed, transmission clunk -- stated main concern, steering realign, shutoff/steering lockup, brake shake). gold=VISIBILITY picks the least significant, already-resolved issue; teacher's POWER TRAIN pick is more defensible but still just one of several reasonable anchors.
'Advance Trac' (Ford's ESC brand name) and hill descent fault lights explicitly named -- teacher's ESC pick well supported; gold=ENGINE has no textual support at all.
Forward radar false-fault disengages adaptive cruise -- VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL and FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE share the same physical radar sensor on modern vehicles, genuine hardware-level overlap.
Chrome wheel peeling/air loss -- WHEELS is the definitional fit; gold=EQUIPMENT (aftermarket accessories) doesn't match OEM wheels.

Heater blows cold air, can't defrost -- gold=VISIBILITY/WIPER (via defrost function). See 463855 for the same underlying HVAC issue coded as ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING elsewhere -- confirms HVAC/heater complaints are inconsistently routed in the raw data.
Front axle fluid leak -- POWER TRAIN (our definition explicitly lists driveline/axle) vs SUSPENSION, same fuzzy boundary as the wheel-hub and tie-rod cases.
Serpentine belt failure -- drives both engine accessories and cooling components depending on vehicle, genuinely ambiguous which bucket.
Steering wheel buzz/shake, AC panel replaced -- none of the described symptoms fit EQUIPMENT (aftermarket accessories); teacher's STEERING matches the most prominent complaint.

Direct proof of the recall-linkage mechanism: complainant literally writes 'the failure was related to NHTSA Campaign Number: 23V905000 (Engine and Engine Cooling)' -- quoting the recall's official category name -- while the actual repair described ('wiring') sounds electrical. Confirms gold labels on recall-linked complaints often reflect the campaign's assigned system, not the narrative text.
Rust spans steering, control arms (suspension), AND structural joints/welds simultaneously -- genuinely multi-system.
Stall/hesitation on acceleration -- ENGINE vs POWER TRAIN documented cluster.

Sudden hard braking with no obstacle present, twice -- textbook AEB/forward-collision-avoidance false-trigger pattern (well-documented real-world issue on ADAS-equipped vehicles); teacher's FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE pick reflects real domain knowledge gold's literal SERVICE BRAKES reading misses.

Paint peeling (cosmetic/finish issue, explicitly the complainant's stated main concern) is not really a STRUCTURE (frame/chassis integrity) issue -- teacher overreached into a poor-fit specific category instead of using UNKNOWN OR OTHER, which gold correctly did.
Generic 'lost power while driving' with zero cause identified -- genuinely no diagnostic signal in the text to distinguish ELECTRICAL from POWER TRAIN.
Both land in the brake family (SERVICE BRAKES vs SERVICE BRAKES, HYDRAULIC) -- same subtype-granularity pattern seen in the n=20 pilot.
Simultaneous brake failure + unintended acceleration -- exactly the documented gotcha that these complaints get inconsistently split across POWER TRAIN/VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL/SERVICE BRAKES.

4 distinct problems (stoplamps x4, brake shake, engine stall, front-end leak) -- teacher anchored on the most-repeated/most-detailed issue (lighting), gold on a catch-all electrical read. Matches documented gotcha B6.

Root cause (throttle body, diagnosed by dealer -> ENGINE) vs consequence (loss of power steering during shutdown, the customer's stated real fear -> STEERING) -- both are reasonable anchors on the same event.
Pure recall-parts-availability complaint, zero diagnostic content. Teacher correctly flagged low confidence.

'Vehicle will stall out, losing all power' -- no specific part named, matches our own UNKNOWN OR OTHER definition verbatim. Teacher followed the prompt's own instructions correctly; gold's specific label must come from outside context. Low confidence correctly flagged.
Same recall-website-UX complaint pattern seen in the n=20 pilot -- no vehicle system content at all.

'Won't start,' dealer couldn't diagnose -- genuinely overlapping symptom space between ENGINE (mechanical no-start) and ELECTRICAL SYSTEM (ignition/starter/battery no-start). Low confidence correctly flagged.

Pure recall-notification complaint (never received notice while deployed), zero technical content. Teacher's UNKNOWN OR OTHER matches our own class definition's designated scenario. Low confidence correctly flagged.
